alerts.label: Cybersecurity / Vendors
alerts.headline: ScreenConnect Incident Prompts Urgent Client and Vendor Checks
alerts.summary: ConnectWise updated its ScreenConnect incident guidance on November 12 after reports of unauthorized access to partner environments. It directs partners to disable identified third-party extensions and verify every technician client runs version 26.6.5 or later; updating the cloud console does not automatically update those clients. Credit unions should obtain confirmation from internal IT and managed-service providers, including whether their endpoints were exposed. Suspected compromised systems require investigation through separate security tools, preserved logs and session revocation. The roughly 400 environments identified had relevant extensions installed; that figure is not a confirmed compromise count.
alerts.impact: Credit-union IT, security and vendor-management teams should confirm extension status and technician-client versions with managed-service providers, assess endpoint exposure, and investigate suspected compromise through separate trusted security tools. Client updates and disabled extensions do not remove an existing compromise.
alerts.sourceDateBasis: Material advisory update, not original publication date.
alerts.freshnessBasis: November 12 update gives newly confirmed technician-client protection and immediate partner actions during an ongoing investigation.
verifiedFacts: The latest update is marked November 12, 2026, 18:45 UTC; original publication is November 11, 2026, 22:45 UTC.
ConnectWise says the endpoint-to-technician spread technique is blocked by ScreenConnect client 26.6.5 or later; cloud-console updates do not automatically update technician clients.
Identified third-party extensions are Labtech Plus, RMM Plus, RMM+, RMM Plus Password Link and RMM+ Password Link.
The approximately 400 environments are those with extensions installed, not a confirmed compromise count.
Vendor guidance includes keeping extensions disabled, revoking active sessions, preserving evidence and using separate security tooling for investigation and remediation.
uncertaintiesAndGuardrails: Do not claim that all 400 environments were compromised.
Do not claim successful endpoint-to-technician propagation; latest advisory says researchers had not observed that spread technique succeed.
Do not describe initial access as a ScreenConnect server/client vulnerability or ConnectWise infrastructure compromise; the vendor says it has no evidence of either.
Cause and full scope remain under investigation. Recheck the live advisory immediately before publication.

alerts.label: Cybersecurity / Infrastructure
alerts.headline: Check Point Discloses Exploited Gateway Attack Chain; Hotfix Urged
alerts.summary: Check Point disclosed on November 12 that attackers chained PHP2Shell with a separate privilege-escalation flaw to compromise unpatched Security Gateways. The observed attacks ran from October 30 through November 4. The vendor recommends installing its November Jumbo Hotfix on Management Servers and Security Gateways. Internet-facing Mobile Access deployments warrant priority review. Credit unions using these products should confirm patch status with their IT teams or providers and review the published compromise indicators. The new disclosure concerns the exploited gateway chain; PHP2Shell fixes had already been available.
alerts.impact: Credit-union security and infrastructure teams using affected Check Point products should verify the vendor-recommended hotfix, prioritize internet-facing Mobile Access systems and investigate relevant compromise indicators. A patch-status check alone does not establish that an earlier intrusion is absent.
alerts.freshnessBasis: New November 12 vendor disclosure and research describe the exploited PHP2Shell plus CVE-2026-123039 gateway chain and publish investigation indicators. The underlying attacks and PHP2Shell fixes are older.
verifiedFacts: PHP2Shell initial access through Mobile Access was followed by CVE-2026-123039 local privilege escalation.
The advisory dates observed exploitation from October 30 through November 4.
Security Gateway and Management security fixes were available October 23.
The vendor recommends the November Jumbo Hotfix on Management Servers and Security Gateways and prioritizing internet-facing Mobile Access deployments.

evidence.verificationMethod: Primary-source search extraction retrieved the full dated advisory and original research; direct opening of the advisory returned an accessibility error.

uncertaintiesAndGuardrails: Do not portray the October 30-November 4 attacks as newly occurring November 12 attacks.
Do not portray October PHP2Shell fixes as newly released November 12 patches.
No exact publication hour is shown.
Advisory solution section contains an unfinished technical-link placeholder; use the working advisory and research URLs rather than that placeholder.
Avoid geographical scope and attribution claims because the advisory and technical research describe different levels of detail.

alerts.label: Cybersecurity / Digital Services
alerts.headline: Apache Releases Fix for Critical HTTP/2 Remote-Code-Execution Flaw
alerts.summary: Apache released HTTP Server 2.4.71 on November 11 to fix three vulnerabilities, including a critical flaw in its HTTP/2 module that can permit remote code execution. CVE-2026-119618 affects HTTP Server versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70; separately distributed mod_h2 releases 2.0.8 through 2.0.42 are also affected. Credit unions should ask hosting and digital-service providers to identify exposed installations and confirm remediation, while internal teams prioritize affected public-facing servers. Apache’s notice identifies the critical risk and fixed release but does not report active exploitation.
alerts.impact: Credit-union technology and vendor-management teams should identify affected Apache installations, prioritize remediation of exposed services and obtain patch evidence from hosting and digital-service providers. Teams using separately distributed mod_h2 should check that component’s affected range as well.
alerts.freshnessBasis: Newly uncovered November 11 critical security release. Eligible as an additional newly uncovered publication; no assumption is made that it was released after the prior November 11 cycle cutoff.
verifiedFacts: Apache’s advisory section is headed Fixed in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 and says Released 2026-11-11.
The release fixes three CVEs: one critical, one important and one low.
CVE-2026-119618 concerns concurrency-related heap corruption in mod_http2 assign_headers() that can lead to remote code execution.
Affected Apache HTTP Server range is 2.4.55 through 2.4.70; affected GitHub mod_h2 releases are 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.
The source records the fix and release on November 11 but makes no active-exploitation claim.

evidence.verificationMethod: Direct primary-source advisory retrieval and find.

uncertaintiesAndGuardrails: Exact release/publication hour is unknown; do not claim this occurred after the prior cycle’s cutoff.
Do not change the source date to November 12 merely because CUAI publishes it then.
Do not claim active exploitation, a CISA KEV listing, or a specific credit-union compromise.
This is a newly uncovered November 11 release, not backfilled older archive content.
